key_insight: The paper turns 3D boxes from vague hints into explicit instructions for image editing. By specifying both the starting and ending boxes, users can directly control object movement and viewpoint changes in real images.
problem_solved: Existing text-based and 2D control methods are often ambiguous for spatial edits, especially when objects move a lot or the camera changes. This work addresses the lack of precise, geometry-aware control for editing real images.
method: Represent each edit as a pair of 3D bounding boxes: an input box and an output box.
Treat the editing task as a well-posed geometric transformation rather than approximate spatial conditioning.
Use structured 3D box specifications to guide realistic object relocation and scene-consistent edits in real images.
impact: This provides a more intuitive and precise control interface for spatial image editing, especially for tasks that are hard to express with text alone. It can help practitioners build more reliable editing systems for AR/VR, content creation, and photo manipulation.

paper_title: Thinking in Boxes: 3D Editing in Real Images Made Easy
paper_authors: Pradhaan S Bhat, Naveen Chandra R, Rishubh Parihar, Vaibhav Vavilala, R. Venkatesh Babu
